title: Quota reset event
description: One discretionary quota reset by an AI vendor. Append-only: once committed, every non-null field except superseded_by is sealed. Corrections are new records that point back via superseded_by.

id.description: <vendor-prefix>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<nn>. Prefix cx = codex, cc = claude-code. Date component is the effective_at date in UTC. Must equal the filename stem.

kind.description: The PRIMARY effect. Retained because it is sealed on every record written before 2026-07-26. Where a record carries `effects`, this must equal effects[0].

effects.description: OPTIONAL, added 2026-07-26 (operator-approved). One vendor announcement routinely carries several distinct quota effects — an immediate reset AND a forward-looking cap removal are different primitives, and `kind` can hold only one. Ordered: effects[0] is the primary effect and must equal `kind`. Non-quota changes shipped in the same announcement (model efficiency gains, redemption-surface changes) are DELIBERATELY not enumerable here — they do not alter allowance — and belong in scope.notes.

effective_at.description: When the reset took effect. RFC 3339, UTC, Z-suffixed.

effective_at_precision.description: How well effective_at is actually known. Never guess a timestamp to look precise — downgrade this instead.

observed_at.description: When we learned of it. Must be >= effective_at.

windows.description: Which quota windows were reset, e.g. weekly, 5h, monthly. Empty array means the window was never established — asserting one we cannot source would be inventing scope.

plans.description: Which subscription plans were affected. Empty array means not established.

partial.description: PREDICATE, fixed 2026-07-26 so this is not re-litigated per record. TRUE iff an ADMISSIBLE source states that the grant reached only some of the accounts otherwise inside scope.plans/scope.windows — a headcount ("500k users"), a percentage, a named cohort, or a staged rollout. FALSE means an admissible source supports universal coverage. NULL means UNESTABLISHED — no source addresses coverage either way. ⚠️ NULL was added 2026-07-26 because a REQUIRED BOOLEAN CANNOT SAY "WE DO NOT KNOW", and that is the root cause of the 2026-07-26 audit: 24 of 29 records carried at least one over-claimed field, and 9 of those were this one field asserting coverage no source addressed. A restriction on WHEN a benefit applied (off-peak hours) or on WHICH WINDOW was reset is NOT partial — only account coverage counts. Note also: if the only source for a restriction is inadmissible under §2's mirror rule, this stays FALSE or NULL even where the restriction is probably real. The field tracks what is sourceable; scope.notes carries the rest.

confidence.description: confirmed = vendor stated it, or sentinel telemetry captured it. probable = multiple independent user reports, consistent timing. reported = single source.

evidence.description: At least one item. A record with no evidence does not exist.

author.description: Named author or handle where there is one, otherwise null.

archive_url.description: Wayback or archive.today copy, once one exists.

superseded_by.description: Null, or the id of the record that corrects this one. On a SEALED record this is the only mutable field.

field_support.description: OPTIONAL, added 2026-07-26. THE ROOT-CAUSE FIX from the audit of that date. Records the PROVENANCE of each enrichment field, separately from its value, because a populated field is otherwise indistinguishable from an asserted one. `attested` = a source states this OF THIS EVENT. `inferred` = it follows from a class-level statement about how the mechanism generally works, or from a neighbouring event — plausible, but nobody asserted it here. `unestablished` = no source addresses it. Absent means the provenance was never recorded, which is the honest reading of every record written before 2026-07-26. The audit found 41 field values across 24 records that were `inferred` or `unestablished` while reading as assertions; this field is what stops that recurring, because filling it in forces the question to be asked.

status.description: OPTIONAL, added 2026-07-26. Absent means "sealed" — every record written before this field existed is sealed, and stays sealed. A "provisional" record is explicitly unsealed: it may still be edited, because it marks a question rather than asserting an answer. Promotion to sealed is one-way.

links.description: OPTIONAL, added 2026-07-26. Typed relations to other records. Exists because `superseded_by` was the only inter-record link and it means "corrected by", which is the wrong semantics for "these two records disagree" or "these came from one announcement".

relation.description: conflicts_with = these records may describe the same underlying event, or contradict each other, and a human must rule. same_announcement_as = one vendor announcement produced both records (see the multi-effect schema defect). related_to = weaker association, stated in the note.
